# tinyux

> Self-hosted UX telemetry, optional aggregate heatmaps, and contextual micro-surveys.
> One static JS file + one collector endpoint. MIT license. v0.2.0.

This file is the implementation contract for AI agents integrating tinyux.

## Files

- Library: https://tanzir71.github.io/tinyuxjs/tinyux.js
- Minified library: https://tanzir71.github.io/tinyuxjs/tinyux.min.js
- Collector: https://tanzir71.github.io/tinyuxjs/collect.php
- Schema: https://tanzir71.github.io/tinyuxjs/schema.sql
- Human docs: https://tanzir71.github.io/tinyuxjs/docs.html

## Integration steps

1. Download `tinyux.js` and serve it from the project's static assets.
2. Add the script tag to product pages:

```html
<script src="/js/tinyux.js"
  data-app-id="APP_ID_HERE"
  data-api-url="/collect.php"
  data-config='{"surveys":{"maxPerSession":2}}'></script>
```

3. Deploy `collect.php` next to `tinyux.js`. It creates its SQLite DB in `tinyux-data/` on the first request (PHP needs write access to that folder) and blocks web access to it with `.htaccess`. On nginx, block the folder or set `TINYUX_DB_PATH` outside the web root. Run `php collect.php --check` to verify. Do not re-run `schema.sql` on an existing database.
4. If the collector runs on a different origin than the pages, add those origins to `$ALLOWED_ORIGINS` in `collect.php`.
5. Add declarative triggers:

```html
<button data-tinyux-trigger="click" data-tinyux-survey-id="upgrade-clarity">
  Upgrade
</button>

<section id="pricing" data-tinyux-trigger="section-scroll" data-tinyux-threshold="0.5" data-tinyux-once="session" data-tinyux-survey-id="pricing-clarity">
</section>
```

6. Register surveys:

```js
const ux = window.tinyux.getInstance()
ux.registerSurvey({
  id: 'pricing-clarity',
  type: 'yesno',
  title: 'Pricing clarity',
  question: 'Did this section answer your question?',
  oncePerSession: true,
  ui: { mode: 'corner', position: 'bottom-right' }
})
```

## Collector contract

The client POSTs JSON batches. Accept `Content-Type: application/json`; also accept `text/plain` bodies sent by `navigator.sendBeacon` on page hide. Parse the body as JSON regardless of content type.

Every event and survey answer has a UUID `id`. Store it and ignore duplicates: retries can deliver the same batch twice. The reference collector uses unique indexes on `(app_id, event_uid)` and `(app_id, survey_uid)` with `INSERT OR IGNORE`.

Request body:

```json
{
  "app_id": "acme-app",
  "client_id": "uuid",
  "session_id": "uuid",
  "user": {
    "id": "user_123",
    "account_id": "acct_456",
    "traits": {"plan": "team"}
  },
  "ts": 1781230000,
  "meta": {
    "url": "https://app.example.com/page",
    "referrer": "",
    "viewport": {"w": 1366, "h": 768},
    "scroll_pct": 45,
    "focus_ms": 12000,
    "interaction_count": 2,
    "click_count": 2,
    "scroll_pct_max": 80,
    "v": "0.2.0",
    "score": 10,
    "user": {
      "id": "user_123",
      "account_id": "acct_456",
      "traits": {"plan": "team"}
    }
  },
  "events": [
    {"id": "3f6b2c1e-...", "type": "interaction", "ts": 1781230001, "meta": {}},
    {"id": "9a0d77c4-...", "type": "heatmap_point", "ts": 1781230001, "meta": {"x_pct": 52, "y_pct": 34, "viewport": "1366x768", "path": "/pricing", "input": "click"}}
  ],
  "surveys": [
    {"id": "c41e09b2-...", "survey_id": "pricing-clarity", "type": "yesno", "response": {"value": true}, "ts": 1781230002, "context": {}}
  ]
}
```

Respond with any 2xx status to acknowledge. Non-2xx or network failures are retried from storage with exponential backoff. `meta.gpc` is `true` when `respectGPC` is on and the browser sent Global Privacy Control.

Event types: `page_view` (`spa: true` adds `path`, `from`, `spa`; bfcache restores add `restored`), `interaction`, `section_view`, `focus`, `blur`, `heartbeat`, `exit_intent`, `heatmap_point`, `rage_click` (adds `clicks`), `dead_click`, `survey_shown`, `survey_submitted`, `survey_closed` (adds `reason`), and any custom `track()` type. `rage_click` and `dead_click` meta has the same coarse `x_pct`, `y_pct`, `viewport`, `path`, and sanitized element fields as `heatmap_point`.

Survey responses are `{"value": ...}`; with a matching `followUp` they are `{"value": ..., "comment": "..."}`.

## JavaScript API

- `tinyux.init(config)` - create a new instance.
- `tinyux.getInstance()` - active singleton.
- `tinyux.autoInit()` - read current script attributes and initialize.
- `tinyux.destroy()` - remove every listener, observer, and timer, then clear the singleton.
- `tinyux.consent(granted)` - consent shortcut for the active instance.
- `tinyux.version` - library version string.
- `instance.track(type, meta)` - queue a custom event.
- `instance.bind(selector, eventName, opts)` - delegated interaction binding.
- `instance.registerSurvey(config)` - register survey by `id` or `survey_id`.
- `instance.showSurvey(idOrConfig)` - show a survey immediately.
- `instance.flush()` - force send.
- `instance.stop()` - stop everything without clearing the singleton.
- `instance.consent(granted)` - `true` persists ids and starts sending; `false` discards buffered data, clears tinyux storage keys, and stops.
- `instance.hasConsent()` / `instance.isActive()` - consent state, and whether this instance is tracking.
- `instance.identify(id, traits)` - associate later payloads with an explicit user/account identity from the host app.
- `instance.clearIdentity()` - remove explicit identity from later payloads.
- `instance.getIdentity()` - read the current explicit identity.
- `instance.on(event, handler)` - subscribe to lifecycle events.

Events: `sent`, `send_error`, `interaction`, `page_view`, `survey_shown`, `survey_submitted`, `survey_closed`, `exit_intent`, `rage_click`, `dead_click`, `consent`.

## Config added in v0.2 (all off or unchanged by default)

- `spa: true` - page views on client-side route changes.
- `frustration: true` or `{enabled, rageClicks: 3, rageWindowMs: 700, rageRadiusPx: 24, deadClickMs: 1000}`.
- `consent: 'granted' | 'pending'` - pending holds events in memory, writes no storage, shows no surveys.
- `storage: 'local' | 'session' | 'none'` - `none` is cookieless.
- `clientIdTtlDays: 395` - anonymous id rotation.
- `respectGPC: false | true | 'all'`.
- `sampleRate: 1` - share of sessions tracked.
- `ui.theme: 'light' | 'dark' | 'auto'`, `ui.labels: {...}`, `ui.nonce: '...'`.
- `heatmaps: true` and `exitIntent: true` shorthands.
- Removed: `mouseSampling`.

## Survey types

- `rating`: numeric buttons, default scale 5 (`min`, `scale`).
- `nps`: 0 to 10 buttons with low/high hints.
- `yesno`: Yes/No buttons.
- `choice`: choices array.
- `text`: textarea. Use sparingly because users can type personal data.

Survey UI:
- Default: blocking center modal.
- Corner: set `ui: { mode: 'corner', position: 'bottom-right' }`.
- Positions: `bottom-right`, `bottom-left`, `top-right`, `top-left`.
- Follow-ups: `followUp: { when: '<=6' | [values] | value, question: '...' }` asks one free-text question when the first answer matches.
- Modals use native `<dialog>` where available; focus returns to the previously focused element. Corner prompts never take focus.

## Identity

tinyux uses anonymous `client_id` and `session_id` by default. Integrators can attach known user/account data:

```js
const ux = window.tinyux.getInstance()
ux.identify('user_123', {
  account_id: 'acct_456',
  plan: 'team',
  role: 'admin'
})
```

Payloads include top-level `user` and `meta.user`. Do not fingerprint browsers or devices to infer identity.

## Optional aggregate heatmaps

Heatmaps are disabled by default. Enable them only when the host app wants aggregate click/tap density:

```html
<script src="/js/tinyux.js"
  data-app-id="APP_ID_HERE"
  data-api-url="/collect.php"
  data-config='{"heatmaps":{"enabled":true}}'></script>
```

Heatmap events are stored as normal `events` rows with `event_type = 'heatmap_point'`. Metadata contains coarse `x_pct` and `y_pct` page coordinates, a viewport bucket, URL path, input type, and sanitized element metadata. tinyux does not capture screenshots, DOM snapshots, mouse trails, or replayable sessions.

## Privacy

By default tinyux does not capture screen contents, screenshots, DOM snapshots, keystroke contents, clipboard contents, camera, microphone, console logs, network logs, mouse trails, or form values. Dataset metadata is filtered by denylist; use `datasetAllowlist` for strict deployments. The reference collector never writes IP addresses to its log; `php collect.php --prune --days=395` enforces retention.
